## Direct answer

To file a POCSO case, you must report the offence to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police, who are required to record the report and take immediate action for the care and protection of the child, including reporting the matter to the Child Welfare Committee and the Special Court within 24 hours [Source 1].

## Why this is the legal position

- Section 19 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 mandates that any person who has knowledge of an offence under the Act must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police [Source 1].

## How this applies to you

- This applies to any individual who has knowledge of or apprehension that an offence under the POCSO Act is likely to be committed or has already been committed, including the child victim [Source 1].

## What you can do now

1. The next step is to report the incident to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police, who will record the report and take immediate action for the care and protection of the child, including reporting the matter to the Child Welfare Committee and the Special Court within 24 hours [Source 1].
